notes: The 10-year US interest rate (4.94%) is 0.78% above the 3-month rate (4.15%), but the gap has shrunk by 0.21% in 3 months: a shrinking gap often comes late in an expansion.
Copper has gained 5.4% on gold over 3 months. Copper follows factory and building demand, while gold is bought in worrying times, so this points to stronger growth.
The US stock market (S&P 500) is below its 200-day (about 10-month) average price: a broad downtrend.

todaysConditions.note: The US dollar has risen 4.3% against major currencies over 3 months. Gains made abroad shrink when converted back to dollars, and countries that borrowed in dollars find the debt harder to repay.
Copper, a gauge of demand for industrial metals, is down 15% over 3 months: bad for markets full of mining companies.
The fear gauge (VIX) is at 23.8, and world stocks are 1.8% below their 200-day (about 10-month) average. Steadier markets then tend to hold up better, and emerging markets suffer most.
Chip-maker shares did 13.9% worse than world stocks over 3 months: a drag on tech-heavy markets.
